subject: A few things I noticed about Murrieta Auto Repair's online presence
body:
Hi there,

I run a small studio that helps local auto shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Murrieta Auto Repair and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- You're ahead of most shops here — you've actually got online "Book an Appointment" and service-estimate forms, which a lot of your competitors don't.
- Strong, steady reputation (~64 Yelp reviews, 4.4) and clear positioning as the dealership alternative.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- Your reputation is invisible on your own site. You've earned 60+ reviews on Yelp and Google, but none of that shows up on murrietaautorepair.net — so someone deciding between you and the shop down the road never sees it.
- No after-hours capture. You're closed Sat/Sun and evenings, so anyone who finds you then either uses the static form (and waits) or moves on. There's no instant callback or 24/7 capture catching those leads while they're hot.
- No live chat. A lot of younger customers won't call — they'll ask a quick question in a chat box or leave.
- Your contact email is a free verizon.net address. Beyond looking dated, those can quietly land in spam when customers email you — worth a branded address on your own domain.

None of this is urgent, and the shop clearly runs well — but each of these is quietly costing you jobs that are already trying to reach you.

If you ever want, I'm happy to walk through how a couple of these could be fixed cheaply. Either way, figured the audit might be useful.

Best,
Leo Lebel
cheddar.lebel@gmail.com

subject: A few things I noticed about Affordable Auto Clinic's online presence
body:
Hi Sam,

I run a small studio that helps local auto shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Affordable Auto Clinic and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- Genuinely strong setup — branded email, free-estimate form, a before/after portfolio, and real brand partnerships (PPG, 3M, SATA). That's better than most body shops out here.
- Excellent reputation: 5.0 across ~85 reviews and BBB A+ accredited.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- That 5.0 reputation is invisible on your own site. All those reviews live on Google, Yelp and Birdeye — but someone landing on aactemecula.com to decide between you and another shop never sees a single one. Pulling them onto the site is one of the highest-leverage, cheapest wins available to you.
- No after-hours capture. You're closed evenings and Sunday, so a fender-bender inquiry at 8pm hits a form and waits — no instant callback catching it while they're deciding.
- No live chat. A lot of estimate-shoppers want a quick answer before they commit to filling out a form.
- The site is missing the behind-the-scenes setup (LocalBusiness markup) that tells Google to surface you for "auto body shop near me" searches — so you're likely ranking below shops doing far worse work.

None of this is urgent, and your work clearly speaks for itself — but each of these is quietly costing you jobs that are already trying to reach you.

If you ever want, I'm happy to walk through how a couple of these could be fixed cheaply. Either way, figured the audit might be useful.

Best,

subject: A few things I noticed about 395 Auto & Performance's online presence
body:
Hi Rene,

I run a small studio that helps local auto and performance shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across 395 Auto & Performance and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- You're doing things most shops don't — a quote-request form, customer testimonials right on the site, and even an instant tire-quote tool. That's a real edge.
- Excellent reputation (Yelp 4.9, CARFAX 5.0), with people specifically calling out your transparency.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- No after-hours capture. You're closed weekends — which is exactly when enthusiasts are thinking about builds and tires. A static form at 9pm Saturday either waits till Monday or loses them to the next shop. A missed oil change is small; a missed build or tune is thousands walking away.
- No live chat. A lot of younger customers won't call — they'll ask a quick question in a chat box or move on.
- The site is missing the behind-the-scenes setup (LocalBusiness markup) that tells Google to surface you for "performance shop near me" searches — so you're likely ranking below shops doing worse work.
- Only a generic info@ inbox is surfaced — fine for now, but it makes it easy for a high-ticket build inquiry to sit unseen.

None of this is urgent, and your reputation clearly speaks for itself — but each of these is quietly costing you jobs that are already trying to reach you.

subject: A few things I noticed about Mr Bill's online presence
body:
Hi Bill,

I run a small studio that helps local auto body shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Mr Bill's Touch Up and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- 25+ years, multiple locations, and mobile auto body repair as a differentiator — that's a real story most shops can't tell.
- Strong outside reputation (Yelp ~98 reviews, Birdeye 4.5 / 100 reviews) and a free-quote form on the site.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- Your hours aren't published anywhere on your own site. Customers genuinely can't tell when you're open without calling — and many won't bother.
- Your phone number isn't on the homepage. It's tucked inside a form, so someone ready to call right now has to dig for it.
- Your reputation is barely visible on your own site. You've got nearly 200 reviews across Yelp and Birdeye, but a visitor deciding between you and another shop sees almost none of it.
- No after-hours capture and no live chat. A collision inquiry at 8pm hits a static form and waits — no instant callback catching it while they're deciding.
- The site itself is a dated multi-page static setup, and it's missing the behind-the-scenes markup that tells Google to surface you for "auto body shop near me" searches.

None of this is urgent, and your work clearly speaks for itself — but each of these is quietly costing you jobs that are already trying to reach you.
